body: An update to the gdextension docs in the manual would be needed as well, since the code examples use some of these functions.

Hm. It's possible that https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/104985 has made it so that there isn't really any performance benefit to constructing a `StringName` directly from a `char *`, since a `String` would be constructed anyway.

But there may still be a performance benefit to having these APIs, because creating a `String` and converting to `StringName` means crossing the GDExtension <-> Godot boundary twice, whereas these APIs mean only crossing it once. We should evaluate how common it is for developers to start from a `char *` and want to create a `StringName`.

I agree that `p_static` is confusing. Whether we deprecate this or not, I think we need to better document that, since it'll still be available even if deprecated.

I wonder if we're still using the `StringName(const char *p_name, bool p_static)` constructor with `p_static` as `true` within the engine itself? If not, we should probably look at removing/deprecating it in the engine as well

I don't have any opinion on the performance side of this discussion.

However as a heavy user of GDExtension, I find really useful to have a straightforward way to create a `StringName` from C.

GDExtension is  already a complex API due to its double level of indirections (to call a method in a Godot object, we need to call function to get function pointer on base tools, then need to call those base tools to get actual function pointer on the méthode we want to call), so adding another hoop to jump through by requesting to manipulate String (and hence having to first call functions to get the function pointers on the string operation functions) is just added cruelty 😁

So even if it turns out we always want to build `StringName` from `String`, I suggest we still keep `gdextension_string_name_new_with_*` as convenient helpers and just replace their internal implementation

> These functions are still needed:
> 
> * `StringName(const char *)` can be faster (about 60%) than `StringName(const String &)` if no `String` exists yet, but a `StringName` entry does exist. This can be relevant depending on the application.

This is a good point. However, applications typically either create temporary StringNames and destroy them, or always cache them. For languages where literals don't use Latin1 encoding, such as C# and Rust, `new_from_latin1` doesn't offer much advantage, as it would cause character loss when converting to StringName.

> * `p_static` is needed because only `StringName` constructed with `p_static=true` are allowed to persist at Godot exit. Otherwise, the engine will complain about orphan `StringName`. This is used quite a lot in the engine, for example for the `SNAME` macro.

The `p_static` only supports Latin1 encoding, which is an unnecessary restriction (causing character loss). Moreover, as a workaround, I can clean up static StringNames in the deinitialization hook to avoid orphans.

> > These functions are still needed:
> > 
> > * `StringName(const char *)` can be faster (about 60%) than `StringName(const String &)` if no `String` exists yet, but a `StringName` entry does exist. This can be relevant depending on the application.
> 
> This is a good point. However, applications typically either create temporary StringNames and destroy them, or always cache them. 

Godot does this quite a lot. Most `StringName`s created by the engine are created on the spot. Whether or not there's a backing `StringName` for it is kind of left up to chance.
Using `SNAME` more often might be a good idea, but currently the source code recommends against it.

> For languages where literals don't use Latin1 encoding, such as C# and Rust, `new_from_latin1` doesn't offer much advantage, as it would cause character loss when converting to StringName.

C++ also doesn't use `latin1` encoding for string literals — it's utf8. See also https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/100641.
We've simply chosen to ignore this potential problem so far, because all our `StringName` are actually ASCII only, and thus latin1 sufficiently covers it.

> > * `p_static` is needed because only `StringName` constructed with `p_static=true` are allowed to persist at Godot exit. Otherwise, the engine will complain about orphan `StringName`. This is used quite a lot in the engine, for example for the `SNAME` macro.
> 
> The `p_static` only supports Latin1 encoding, which is an unnecessary restriction (causing character loss). Moreover, as a workaround, I can clean up static StringNames in the deinitialization hook to avoid orphans.

Like with the above point, most, if not all, `StringName` created by english programmers are ASCII only. Therefore, the `latin1` bindings are by far the most important. In contrast, users' `StringName`s are cached (and released) in the way you suggest. But this is difficult to achieve in low level languages: Our own code base currently struggles with a proper release order on shutdown.
That being said, if static non-latin1 `StringName` are needed, there could be a PR for this.

Many translation related APIs use StringName and can contain non-latin1 characters. It would be surprising if a StringName created with `p_static=true` does not match the original text.

I'm not sure if we should expose `p_static` or deprecate it and let users manage it themselves. In fact, this parameter was not exposed before #78580, and seems no one asked for it.

I found godot-dotnet seem to have been troubled by `p_static` as well https://github.com/raulsntos/godot-dotnet/issues/20, but I don't know if godot-dotnet needs the parameter.

I think it would be good to get some input from @raulsntos.
